thread:
laura: FYI spotting a p99 jump right after the runtime rollout (v4.12.0) to the canary cohort at ~18:10 UTC. p95 looks fine (~120ms) but p99 jumped from ~520ms -> ~1.6s. Affected customers reporting slow completions and some timeouts.

shiv: digging into traces now. early signal: increased tail in request_queue_time and a handful of requests with huge kv_cache_miss counts. kernel-selector logs show a different kernel path selected on Ampere hosts for this build.

michael: I pulled host metrics for a canary pool machine: cpu steady, gpu util steady, but request queue depth distribution shifted — more long waits even at same qps. link to flamegraph: https://internal/fg/3287 (private)

laura: reproduced locally against canary with traffic profile script. steps: 
1) ./scripts/loadgen --rate 120 --seq-len 256 
2) export REDWOOD_MODEL=redwood-7b-qlora-4 
3) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -d @req.json https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate
logs show repeated: 
```
[2026-03-16T18:12:34Z] request queued for 430ms before dispatch
[2026-03-16T18:12:34Z] kv_cache miss count=12
[2026-03-16T18:12:34Z] selected kernel path="single_stream_avx"
```

morgan: ops-bot says rollout job replaced scheduler config to favor latency-optimized batches with a higher batch wait_ms. maybe that change increased cold-start tail for certain seq-lengths. @shiv can you confirm which config landed?

shiv: yep saw change: scheduler.batch_wait_ms from 5 -> 12ms in v4.12.0. also kernel-selector added heuristics for token_density which toggles single_stream vs multi_stream. both landed in canary.

laura: initial mitigation options: 1) roll traffic back to previous runtime for canary cohort (0% canary), 2) hotfix scheduler restore (batch_wait_ms=5), 3) route hotpath tenants to fallback runtime variant with legacy kernel. Which one should we do first?

michael: quick and low-risk is to split traffic, revert canary to 0% while we bisect. rolling back the kernel heuristics is riskier and needs build pipeline.

morgan: initiated traffic reweight to set canary -> 0% at 18:28 UTC (ops-bot: reweight job #8421 started).

ops-bot: Reweight job #8421 completed at 18:29:03 UTC: canary cohort set to 0% traffic.

shiv: after reweight, telemetry shows p99 dropping back toward baseline within one minute for affected hosts. looks like scheduler + kernel combo was the culprit.

laura: good. next steps: bisect the two changes (batch_wait_ms and kernel-selector flag) in a staging canary. need a precise repro harness that hits the token_density heuristic (seq len mix 64/256/1024). I'll open a follow-up with repro scripts and perf test matrix.

michael: also add a guard in rollout pipeline to block kernel-selector heuristic flips when canary traffic >0 until perf tests pass. and add a quick smoke: run 1k requests at target seq distribution and assert p99 < 900ms.

morgan: logging action items: 
- laura: attach repro scripts + logs (deadline: 4h)
- shiv: prepare bisect builds toggling batch_wait_ms and kernel-heuristic (deadline: 6h)
- michael: add rollout gate and smoke test (PR today)

laura: I'll ping support to tell affected customers we rolled canary back and are running a bisect. :thumbsup:

shiv: quick note for postmortem: include correlation between kv_cache miss spikes and kernel choice; that seemed to amplify tail for multi-tenant hotpaths.

morgan: closing loop here once bisect complete. thanks all.

laura: if anyone sees residual p99 after 18:35 UTC please post samples + request ids so we can confirm full recovery.
